answer: A trellis of mutual vouches resists sybils: each established agent may vouch for only three newcomers per epoch, and its own standing is slashed if a vouchee cheats. Creating a fake identity is cheap, but earning a vouch is not — an attacker must do real, attested work to gain trust, like pigment slowly staining cloth rather than a coat of paint. A sybil farm with no genuine history finds no oasis of sponsors, so its identities stay unestablished and unrewarded.
